title: Bridgewell Homeowner Service Contracts: Enrollment Eligibility, Term Dates and Start of Coverage
content:
**Who may enroll.** Enrollment in Homeowner Service Contracts is open only to owner-occupied residential properties whose property type and living-area square footage satisfy the entry gate of the tier purchased. Properties rented to tenants or used commercially are enrolled under rental property service contracts instead, and the property type and square footage are taken from the customer's statement at enrollment.

The entry gate is the same on all six tiers (Bridgewell ApplianceCare, Bridgewell SystemsCare and Bridgewell HomeCare Bronze, Silver, Gold and Platinum):

| Entry gate element | Every tier |
|---|---|
| Property types | single-family home, townhome, condominium, mobile home |
| Maximum living-area square footage | 9999 |
| Occupancy | owner-occupied |

**Elections at enrollment.** The service call fee elected must be one of the tier's lower fee option, standard service call fee or higher fee option, and billing is either monthly or annual.

**Term dates.** Each term lasts the tier's contract term in calendar months. The term end date is the day before the same calendar day that many months later, falling back to the last day of the month when that day does not exist. *Hypothetical:* a 12-month term starting on January 15 ends on January 14 of the following year.

**Start of coverage — online or phone enrollment.** For an online or phone enrollment, the coverage effective date is the start date plus the tier's waiting period in calendar days, and the contract stays in its waiting period until then. For an online or phone enrollment, the contract activates no earlier than the waiting period's number of calendar days after the contract is purchased, counting the purchase date as day zero.

- The clock starts from the purchase, as recorded by the contract's start date.
- Day zero is the purchase date itself; the comparison is "not earlier than", and the day that completes the count does qualify.
- *Boundary pair, hypothetical, with a 30-day waiting period:* a contract purchased on March 1 (day zero) may activate on March 31 (day 30); it may not activate on March 30 (day 29).

**Start of coverage — conversion from a real estate contract.** A conversion enrollment continues a real estate contract held by the same customer for the same property address, has its coverage effective date equal to its start date and activates immediately. A conversion enrollment keeps continuous coverage only when its start date is no later than the conversion continuity window (in calendar days) after the day the real estate contract term ends; the day count starts the day after the real estate term end date and the boundary day itself qualifies. A conversion requested later than that is enrolled as a phone enrollment with the normal waiting period.

| Conversion start date, hypothetical, real estate term ending June 10, 30-day window | Day count | Result |
|---|---|---|
| June 11 | day 1 | continuous coverage, active immediately |
| July 10 | day 30 (boundary) | continuous coverage, active immediately |
| July 11 | day 31 | enrolled as a phone enrollment with the normal waiting period |

The waiting-period date and the real estate term end date are read from the system records; the property type and square footage are the customer's own statement at enrollment.
